key_insight: A machine-learning pipeline can identify ferromagnetic vs antiferromagnetic order and estimate magnetization from non-magnetic material descriptors, enabling rapid screening of 2D magnetic candidates.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports faster discovery of spintronic materials by prioritizing compounds likely to exhibit antiferromagnetism or skyrmion-like magnetic textures without requiring explicit magnetic descriptors.
method: LightGBM classifier using structure-derived fixed-length descriptors for FM vs AFM labeling.
Residual MLP regressor with compositional, structural, electronic, and task-specific initial-state descriptors for magnetization prediction.
Log-transformed targets, robust weighted loss, and a 3-model ensemble for stable regression; magnetic imaging and phase reconstruction used on selected candidates.
evidence_signal: Grouped five-fold cross-validation and isolated testing yielded 93.6% balanced accuracy for magnetic-order classification, while magnetization prediction achieved 0.686 μB/formula unit mean absolute error.
watch_item: Performance may depend on Materials Project coverage and careful chemical-group splitting; deploying the model on out-of-distribution chemistries or noisy descriptors could reduce reliability.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Identification of Magnetic Orders and Skyrmions
